focus: 壞消息追到已交付的資料
lead: 今天練的是已經交出去的東西出錯了怎麼升級：資料在客戶手上、而且你上次報的數字是錯的。心法 —— 先劃出受影響範圍，再劃出「沒有」受影響的範圍，主動提出更正，不要等對方發現。每個 speaking 段落請先出聲講完再看 model answer。

phrases.en: Let me start with the bad news, then what we're doing about it.
phrases.gl: 我先講壞消息，再講處理方式（先宣告順序，聽的人就不會覺得被埋伏）
phrases.ex: Let me start with the bad news, then what we're doing about it — last Friday's drop went out with bad cut-in labels.

phrases.en: Here's what's affected — and here's what isn't.
phrases.gl: 劃出受影響的範圍，也劃出沒受影響的範圍（止血的關鍵一句，避免對方以為全垮了）
phrases.ex: Here's what's affected: 25k highway frames from the June batch. Here's what isn't: every night and urban frame we've shipped.

phrases.en: I need to correct a number I gave you.
phrases.gl: 我要更正上次報過的數字（自己更正，比被抓到強一百倍）
phrases.ex: I need to correct a number I gave you at the last review — the 91% cut-in recall was measured against labels we now know are wrong.

phrases.en: We found it in our own QA sampling.
phrases.gl: 是我們自己抽檢抓到的（說明控制力還在我們手上，不是被客戶打臉）
phrases.ex: We found it in our own QA sampling on Tuesday night, not from the customer's evaluation.

phrases.en: My confidence on that is about X%.
phrases.gl: 把不確定量化（比「應該還好」可信太多，也保護了你自己）
phrases.ex: My confidence that the night set is clean is about 90% — the full re-check finishes Friday.

phrases.en: If I'm wrong about the scope, it's wrong on the high side.
phrases.gl: 如果範圍估錯，會是往哪一邊錯（誠實交代誤差方向，避免二次爆雷）
phrases.ex: If I'm wrong about the scope, it's wrong on the high side — 25k frames is my worst case, not my best case.

phrases.en: I'd like to get ahead of it with the customer.
phrases.gl: 我想主動先跟客戶說（把揭露變成你的提案，而不是被迫的動作）
phrases.ex: I'd like to get ahead of it with the customer today, rather than have their team hit it in evaluation on Monday.

phrases.gl: 這是我們沒接住（廠商出錯，但責任在你這邊；把鍋推給廠商會讓對方對你失去信任）
phrases.ex: The vendor rotated in a new labeling team in June and we didn't re-run acceptance sampling. That was our miss.
phrases.fix: 取代 “It's the vendor's problem, not ours”

phrases.en: Here's the correction, and here's when you'll have it.
phrases.gl: 更正內容和交付時間一起講（把「我再確認」升級成一個承諾）
phrases.ex: Here's the correction, and here's when you'll have it: the relabeled batch Tuesday, the revised metrics Wednesday.
phrases.fix: 取代 “We will double check and update you later”

setup: Setup. On Tuesday night your QA sampling found that roughly 18% of the cut-in labels in the 25k highway frames from the June batch are wrong. The labeling vendor rotated a new team onto your project in mid-June and nobody re-ran acceptance sampling on the first batch after the change. Those frames went out to the customer in last Friday's data drop, and the 91% cut-in recall you reported at the milestone review was measured against them. Grace, from the customer program office, expects her team to start a clean evaluation on Monday — and David, the program manager, is hearing about this from you for the first time this morning.

prompts.q: You open with David. He thinks last Friday's drop went out clean.
prompts.frame: Announce the order → what's affected, with a number → what isn't affected → how you found it → the one thing you don't know yet.
prompts.say: 先出聲講完整段（目標 40 秒），不要用道歉開場，也不要先講廠商的事。
prompts.model: “David, let me start with the bad news, then what we're doing about it. Here's what's affected: the 25k highway frames from the June batch — our QA sampling says about 18% of the cut-in labels on those are wrong. They went to the customer in Friday's drop. Here's what isn't affected: everything night and urban, and everything we shipped before June, because that was all labeled by the original team. We found it in our own QA sampling on Tuesday night, not from the customer. What I don't know yet is whether the lane-change labels drifted the same way — that sample finishes Friday, and my confidence they're clean is around 90%. If I'm wrong on the scope, it's wrong on the high side.”

prompts.q: David: “Hold on. You told the steering committee 91% recall two weeks ago. Was that number wrong?”
prompts.frame: Answer yes plainly → say what the number really means now → own the process gap in one sentence → say what has already changed → give the date for the corrected number.
prompts.say: 出聲練習「更正自己報過的數字」——承擔一句就好，不要連續道歉，30 秒內講完。
prompts.model: “Yes — I need to correct that number. The 91% was measured against the June labels, so it's not trustworthy for the highway cut-in slice. My honest read is the real number is lower, but I'm not going to guess at it in this room. The gap is on our side: the vendor rotated a new team onto us in mid-June and we didn't re-run acceptance sampling after the change. That was our miss, and acceptance sampling is now mandatory on the first batch after any team change. I'll have a corrected recall figure Wednesday, once the relabeled batch is back. Until then I'd rather we stop quoting 91% anywhere.”

prompts.q: Grace, on the call an hour later: “So the data we've been planning our whole evaluation around is bad. That's a week of my team's time.”
prompts.frame: Take the hit without arguing → bound the damage precisely → give the recovery with dates → offer something that protects her week → ask for one decision.
prompts.say: 出聲講一次「面對生氣的利害關係人」——不要防守，也不要過度道歉。
prompts.model: “That's a fair reaction, and you're right that it costs your team time — I'm not going to talk you out of that. Let me bound it, though. It's the highway cut-in labels in the June batch, about 25k frames. The night set, the urban set, and everything you got before June are unaffected, so roughly 80% of what's on your side is still good to evaluate. Recovery: the vendor is relabeling that batch under the corrected taxonomy at their cost, we get it back Tuesday, and I'll ship you a replacement drop plus revised metrics Wednesday. To protect Monday, I'd suggest your team starts on the night and urban sets, which were the harder ones anyway, and picks up highway on Wednesday — that way you lose two days, not a week. What I need from you is a decision today: do you want the replacement as a delta drop, or the whole set re-issued? The delta is faster, but it's on you to merge it.”

fixes.bad: According to my understanding, the vendor change the QA team in last month.
fixes.good: As I understand it, the vendor changed the QA team last month.
fixes.note: Tense + preposition：有明確過去時間就要用過去式 changed；last month 前面不加 in。另外 according to my understanding 是翻譯腔，口語用 as I understand it 更自然。

fixes.bad: We found this issue in Wednesday night, the impact to customer is very serious.
fixes.good: We found this on Wednesday night, and the impact on the customer is significant.
fixes.note: Preposition + article：星期幾用 on，不用 in；impact 搭配的是 on，不是 to；customer 前面要 the。very serious 在壞消息場合容易讓人恐慌，significant 精準又不失重量。

fixes.bad: I will responsible for this and give you update tomorrow.
fixes.good: I'll take responsibility for this and give you an update tomorrow.
fixes.note: Word form + article：responsible 是形容詞，不能直接接在 will 後面（要說 I'll be responsible 或 I'll take responsibility）；update 是可數名詞，要加 an。

fixes.bad: Almost 20% label are wrong, it's very very bad news for us.
fixes.good: Almost 20% of the labels are wrong. That's a real problem for the June batch.
fixes.note: Plurals + register：百分比後面接 of the + 複數（20% of the labels）；very very 這種疊字會削弱專業度，直接說明它為什麼是問題就好。

fixes.bad: We should inform customer as soon as possible, otherwise they will discover by themselves.
fixes.good: I'd like to get ahead of it with the customer today, before their team hits it in evaluation.
fixes.note: Article + register：customer 前面要 the。inform / as soon as possible 是公文腔而且沒有時間點；換成第一人稱的提案加上具體的今天，你聽起來就是在主導，而不是在請示。

challenge:
今天在真實會議或訊息中做這一件事：挑一件已經送出去、但你不完全放心的東西，主動先劃範圍 ——

“Let me start with the bad news, then what we're doing about it. Here's what's affected: ___. Here's what isn't: ___. That was our miss. Here's the correction, and here's when you'll have it: ___.”

錄音作業（60 秒，手機錄）：假設你上次報的一個數字是錯的，用英文練習一次更正。

  • 必須明講「這個數字要更正」（I need to correct a number I gave you），不能含糊帶過
  • 必須劃出「沒有受影響」的範圍，並附一個比例或數字
  • 承擔只講一句（That was our miss），然後立刻轉向已經改掉的流程
  • 結尾必須是「更正內容 + 交付日期」，不能是 we will double check
  • 禁用：very very、according to my understanding、as soon as possible、連續兩次以上的 sorry
check: 我有沒有主動說出「我要更正上次那個數字」，而不是等別人發現？
我講壞消息的時候，有沒有同時劃出「沒有受影響」的那一塊，讓對方不會以為全垮了？
面對情緒反應時，我是繼續道歉，還是把範圍、日期和一個要對方決定的問題端上桌？
